step: Open the dashboard. Note which of MER, CAC and conversion breached, and by how much.
In each ad platform, sort campaigns by spend. List any with spend above 2x target CAC and no purchases.
Check creative fatigue: frequency above 3.5, or click-through rate down more than 25% vs the prior 14 days.
Compare platform-reported purchases with Shopify orders for the last 7 days. A gap above 25% means check the pixel and Conversions API.
Check traffic quality: mobile vs desktop conversion, page speed, and whether any advertised product is out of stock.
Pause the waste, move about 20% of budget from the worst to the best campaign, and queue 2 new creatives.
Set a recheck in 48 hours and post a summary in the team channel.
In Shopify, filter orders that are on hold, unfulfilled for 48 hours or more, or payment pending.
For fraud-flagged orders, check address mismatch, repeated cards and unusual quantities. Approve or cancel each.
For orders stuck in fulfilment, contact the warehouse or 3PL and find out why (stock, picking, carrier).
Message affected customers with a new delivery estimate using the saved template.
Tag resolved orders 'exception-resolved' and note the cause.
If three or more orders share one cause, open a fix ticket.
Export refunds from the last 14 days. Tag each by reason.
Group by SKU. Flag any SKU with a refund rate above 8% or three or more refunds with the same reason.
If the reason is damaged in transit: check carrier, packaging and supplier batch. Ask 3 customers for photos.
If the reason is not as described: compare the product page photos and copy with the real product. Fix the page.
Decide the action: pause ads to the SKU, change packaging, or switch carrier. Record the owner and date.
Update the support macro and FAQ for this issue.
Add findings and cost impact to the weekly review.
List every SKU below its reorder point. Calculate days of cover: stock divided by average daily units over the last 14 days.
Mark any SKU where days of cover is shorter than supplier lead time as urgent.
Request a quote and confirm lead time from the supplier.
Raise the purchase order. Record PO number, quantity and expected arrival.
For urgent SKUs, reduce ad spend on the product and add 'ships in X days' or backorder messaging.
Update the reorder point if demand has changed.
Confirm the product page: photos, copy, size guide, price and shipping info.
Test checkout end to end on mobile with a real discount code.
Confirm inventory counts and set the reorder point.
Schedule email, SMS and social posts.
Brief support on FAQs, returns policy and macros.
Set launch ad budgets and creatives. Add UTM tags.
Add launch KPIs to the dashboard and book a 24-hour review.
At 24 hours, review sales, conversion and issues. Decide what to change.
Review the customer's order and ticket history.
Set severity. P1: chargeback, legal or safety. P2: repeated failure or high value. P3: everything else.
Reply within 2 hours for P1 and 8 hours for P2.
Offer a resolution within approved limits (refund, replacement or credit).
Log the outcome and a root-cause tag.
Follow up in 3 days.
Open the dashboard and compare the last 7 days with the prior 7.
Review each KPI marked as a breach. Confirm an open task exists for it.
Review open tasks. Close, reassign or re-date anything overdue.
Review last week's experiment: result and decision.
Choose one priority and one experiment for this week.
Post the summary in the team channel.
Create accounts with role-based access: Shopify, email, chat, password manager, dashboard.
Share the company overview, brand voice guide and product catalogue.
Walk through the dashboard: what each KPI means and what the thresholds are.
Shadow each SOP assigned to the role once.
Complete one SOP independently with a reviewer's sign-off.
Acknowledge each SOP in the SOP system.
Book the 30-day check-in.
